kyoto_so_kawahigashi.gf_detail: Ask. Japanese small plates, clay-pot rice, tempura, fried hamo and grilled fu with butter and soy; no gluten information is published (2025–2026 reviews).
kyoto_so_kawahigashi.vegan_detail: Ask. Vegetable-rich Kyoto-style dishes and earlier wild-herb vegetable broths, but fish and meat are served too; nothing vegan is marked (2024–2026 reviews).
kyoto_so_kawahigashi.hours_raw: Tuesday–Thursday dinner 17:30–21:00, à la carte without reservations, as 膳いぬい; Friday and Saturday lunch 12:00–14:00, an 8-course menu by reservation only, as 刻toki (Tabelog; official site). Closed Sunday and Monday. Bookings via TableCheck up to two months ahead (official site). No service charge listed (Tabelog). 9 seats at a U-shaped counter (13 with event tables); private hire up to 20; non-smoking; cards, transit IC, iD, QUICPay and PayPay (Tabelog). On Marutamachi-dori east of the Kamo River, about 3 min from exit 4 of Jingu-Marutamachi Stn (official site). Opened 25 October 2019 (official site; Tabelog). Lunch udon service ended with a renovation in January 2025 (March 2025 review).
kyoto_so_kawahigashi.notes: [Japanese · Marutamachi by the Kamo, a nine-seat shared counter] A small U-shaped counter east of the Kamo River where two cooks take turns: Tuesday to Thursday evenings bring Inui's gentle Kyoto dinners — clay-pot rice, seasonal small plates, roast beef, with Japanese sake, wine and whisky — no booking needed; Friday and Saturday lunch is a reserved eight-course menu from the Nakahigashi side. Simple, careful seasoning. Closed Sunday and Monday.

roles: Owner chef and culinary director (刻toki, Friday–Saturday)
Kazuhiro Inui (いぬい) cooks Tuesday–Thursday as 膳いぬい
chef_bio.background: Per the official site: born in Kyoto into a family of restaurateurs, trained under the chef’s father at 草喰なかひがし from the age of 12, then worked at the vegan restaurant Kajitsu in New York from 2011; founded One Rice One Soup Inc. in the US in 2016 and One Rice One Soup株式会社 in Japan in 2019 (the invoice holder); based in New York and Kyoto; opened this counter on 25 October 2019. A December 2025 reviewer calls the chef the third son of Hisashi Nakahigashi of 草喰なかひがし. Kazuhiro Inui runs the Tuesday–Thursday dinners.
chef_bio.philosophy: Per the official site: a flat, welcoming place for anyone who loves to eat and drink, where people keep coming back; per a December 2025 review, "so" stands for origin and essence and for the seasoning order sa-shi-su-se-so.
chef_bio.specialty: Clay-pot rice and seasonal small plates.

anecdotes.text: An August 2025 diner on an Inui night ordered à la carte with Ichiro’s Malt whisky, and Inui came over to chat.
A June 2025 guest went back for seconds of the clay-pot rice.
A January 2025 visitor ate a New Year special: ramen made as Kyoto white-miso zoni, with Ohara vegetables and a round mochi.

chef_bio.japanese_sources_summary: 公式サイト: そ/s/KAWAHIGASHI、おいしいを見つける9席のカリナリーハブ、左京区丸太町通川端東入ル東丸太町18-5、京阪神宮丸太町駅4番出口から徒歩約3分、金・土は「刻toki」、火〜木は「膳いぬい」(日本酒と日本ワインのやさしい和食の夜)、オーナーシェフ 中東篤志 (京都の料亭の家に生まれ12歳から父の草喰なかひがしで修業、2011年からニューヨークのヴィーガンレストラン Kajitsu、2016年米国で One Rice One Soup Inc.、2019年 One Rice One Soup株式会社を設立)、2019年10月25日オープン、予約は TableCheck で2か月先まで。食べログ: 日本料理・居酒屋、火〜木17:30〜21:00 (アラカルト、予約不要)、金・土12:00〜14:00 (予約制、8品のコース)、日月定休、U字カウンター9席、禁煙、カード・電子マネー・PayPay 可、インボイス T4130001064399 (One Rice One Soup株式会社)。口コミ (2024〜2026年、英語): 一汁三菜・五菜の定食 (土鍋ご飯付き3,900円)、ローストビーフ、とうもろこしの天ぷら、鱧のフライ、焼き麩のバター醤油、京都の日本酒、イチローズモルト、2025年1月の改装で昼のうどんは終了。

kyoto_ohagi_tomoeya.notes: [Sweets · Toji west gate, ohagi to take away] A tiny shop among the houses behind Toji, where a couple make just two kinds of ohagi each morning — chunky red bean, and kinako with bean paste hidden inside — at ¥200 apiece. kyoto_mati_shogoin.gf_detail: Not gluten-free: a bakery wine bar — croissants, focaccia, bread plates, bruschetta, open sandwiches (2026 reviews).
kyoto_mati_shogoin.vegan_detail: Ask. Vegetable appetizers, a burdock salad and plain breads appear alongside pâté, ham, fish and butter pastries; ingredients are not described (2026 reviews).
kyoto_mati_shogoin.hours_raw: Monday, Tuesday, Saturday and Sunday 12:00–19:00; Friday 16:00–21:00; closed Wednesday and Thursday (Tabelog; hours may change). No reservations (Tabelog). Cards, e-money and PayPay (Tabelog). 7 table seats plus a standing area — a counter and three tables, with standing space up a steep stair on the second floor (Tabelog; March and June 2026). kyoto_mati_shogoin.notes: [Bread and wine · Shogoin near Kawabata-Marutamachi] A small bakery-bar off the main street where you drink natural wine with bread baked on site — flaky croissants, focaccia, an open sandwich of the day’s fish, bruschetta piled with sea bream — plus pâté and roast ham. A few tables and a standing area upstairs; afternoons from noon, Friday evenings. Some find it pricey.

chef_bio.background: An August 2026 regular chatted with the staff, “skilled bakers making bread for the next day right in front of me”. A June 2026 visitor found the bread decent but the prices high, and was bothered by guests passing the second-floor standing area on the way to the third floor.

anecdotes.text: A July 2026 regular on a seventh visit had the day’s katsuo open sandwich with a Dennis Wolf white.
A July 2026 visitor, turned away by crowds at Kibune, found the bar on a search for somewhere to drink nearby.

kyoto_el_bogavante_346.gf_detail: Ask. Tabelog lists gluten-free options, but no dish is named; paella (rice) is the specialty, alongside ajillo with bread, croquettes and other tapas (Tabelog; 2025–2026 reviews).
kyoto_el_bogavante_346.vegan_detail: Ask. Tabelog lists vegetarian options; alioli potatoes and vegetable dishes appear, but stocks for paella are seafood-based (Tabelog; 2025–2026 reviews).
kyoto_el_bogavante_346.hours_raw: Lunch 12:00–15:00 (last entry 14:00; food L.O. 14:00), dinner 17:30–22:00 (last entry 21:00; food L.O. 21:00); closed Wednesday, with summer and winter breaks (Tabelog). Take-away: order by the day before, 11:00–20:30; pickup 12:00–15:00 and 17:30–21:00 (Tabelog). Reservations accepted; fills quickly (April 2025); paella takes about 30 minutes (April 2025). Cards, IC, e-money and QR (Tabelog). 24 seats with counter, a semi-private room for 8 and a terrace; smoking only on the terrace; pets on the terrace in a cart (Tabelog). Children of primary-school age at dinner; preschoolers also welcome at lunch (Tabelog). Wheelchair accessible; free Wi-Fi; sommelier (Tabelog). On Sanjo just west of Nishinotoin, 10 min from Karasuma Oike Stn exit 6 (Tabelog).
kyoto_el_bogavante_346.notes: [Spanish · Sanjo-Nishinotoin, paella and tapas] A bright Spanish gastrobar with a counter, a semi-private room and a terrace, where a Barcelona-trained chef turns out paella in individual pans — squid ink, lobster, kinmedai seafood — plus ajillo, croquettes, cured ham and a tableside crème brûlée, with a sommelier’s list of Spanish wines. Paella lunches from about ¥2,500; dinner course ¥4,800. Book ahead; closed Wednesdays.

chef_bio.background: Tabelog’s shop text: dishes by a chef trained in Barcelona, Spain, and a sommelier-selected list of Spanish wines. The official site’s title reads 「スペイン政府公認優良スペインレストラン」. Invoice T1130001034702 is registered to 株式会社カナルトレス (NTA register). A February 2026 diner returned after several decades away.
chef_bio.philosophy: “Restaurant-quality tapas” (Tabelog shop text).

anecdotes.text: An April 2025 diner was told the paella would take about 30 minutes, so ordered it first.
A May 2026 guest watched the crème brûlée, hiding fruit and ice cream, caramelised at the table.

kyoto_rokusei_okazaki.gf_detail: Ask. Seasonal Kyoto cuisine — the teoke bento of many small dishes, sashimi, dobin-mushi, hamo, eel rice, Omi beef; soy sauce and dashi throughout; no gluten information (official site; 2024–2026 reviews).
kyoto_rokusei_okazaki.vegan_detail: Not vegan: dashi-based Kyoto cuisine with fish and beef (2024–2026 reviews).
kyoto_rokusei_okazaki.hours_raw: Lunch 11:30–14:00 (arrive by 14:00); dinner 17:00–21:00 by reservation only (arrive by 18:00); Soufflé & Café 茶庭 14:00–18:00 (L.O. 17:00); closed Mondays (open on holidays) and some Wednesdays (Tabelog; official site). November 2026: closed 2, 9, 16 and 30 November; lunch only on 24 November; evenings may be cancelled, so always book (official site). Reservations by phone or TableCheck (official site). Service charge 10%, 15% for private rooms and exclusive use (Tabelog, original サービス料１０％ 個室利用・貸切の場合は１５％); private rooms from the “Hana” course ¥10,120 (old wing) or “Chokyu” ¥12,650 (new wing), tax and service included (Tabelog). Cards (VISA, Master, JCB, Diners, UnionPay); no e-money or QR (Tabelog). 250 seats: counter, tatami and sunken seating, five private rooms, two banquet halls and a wedding venue (Tabelog). Seven parking spaces, first come, height 1.9 m (official site). English menu; children’s meals from ¥1,100, baby beds and chairs (Tabelog). Non-smoking, smoking area outside (Tabelog). West of Heian Shrine north of the Biwa canal, 10 min from Higashiyama Stn (Tabelog; October 2026). Founded 1899 (Tabelog).
kyoto_rokusei_okazaki.notes: [Kyoto cuisine · Okazaki by Heian Shrine, since 1899] A large old Kyoto restaurant west of Heian Shrine, known for its teoke bento — a cedar tub of seasonal small dishes, the tubs made by a Living National Treasure — at lunch (about ¥4,000–6,000), with kaiseki in private rooms, a soufflé café in the afternoon, and dinner by reservation only. A favourite before or after the KYOCERA Museum or a shrine visit. 10% service charge.

chef_bio.background: Tabelog’s shop note gives the founding year as 1899 and calls the teoke tubs the work of the Living National Treasure Kiyoshi Nakagawa, of Kiso cedar aged several years. The official site trademarks 「手をけ弁当」. A limited course was offered in October 2026 in connection with the group SixTONES, and an October 2026 guest was seated in a room the group had used.

anecdotes.text: An October 2026 driver arrived before 11:00 for the first-come parking and found staff guiding cars in.
A July 2026 couple on a tour watched the Gion Festival from an air-conditioned room on the same tour itinerary that included lunch here.

kyoto_kyotofu_fujino_isetan.gf_detail: Ask. Tofu dishes — oboro tofu, yudofu, kuzu tofu, sesame tofu, yuba sashimi — are eaten with soy-based sauces and dashi; agedashi tofu, nama-fu dengaku and a soy-milk baumkuchen contain wheat (2026 reviews).
kyoto_kyotofu_fujino_isetan.vegan_detail: Ask. Mostly tofu, yuba and vegetables, but broths and sauces are not described and dashi is likely; the sets include pickles and seasoned rice (2026 reviews).
kyoto_kyotofu_fujino_isetan.hours_raw: 11:00–22:00 (L.O. 21:15); closures follow JR Kyoto Isetan (Tabelog). Reservations accepted, but not for the same day (Tabelog); walk-ins take a numbered ticket, with waits of 15–30 minutes at lunch (July–October 2026). Cards and QR codes; no e-money (Tabelog). 52 seats at tables, window seats with a view of the city; non-smoking; wheelchair accessible (Tabelog; 2026 reviews). Fujino tofu is also sold on Isetan B2F (July 2026). JR Kyoto Isetan 11F, directly connected to Kyoto Station (Tabelog).
kyoto_kyotofu_fujino_isetan.notes: [Tofu · Kyoto Station, Isetan 11F] The restaurant of the Kitano tofu maker Fujino, on Isetan’s restaurant floor with window views over Kyoto: tofu sets built around warm oboro tofu you can refill, with kuzu tofu, agedashi, yuba and a ginger-aburaage rice, about ¥3,000 at lunch, plus yudofu courses. Take a numbered ticket at lunch; no same-day bookings. Fujino tofu to take home is sold on B2F.

roles: Operated by 京とうふ藤野株式会社 (official site)
chef_bio.background: The Tabelog listing links to the site of 京とうふ藤野株式会社, a tofu maker in Kitano, Kyoto, that makes its tofu from 100% Japanese soybeans. A Tabelog Kyoto name search shows the company’s other listings: the main shop’s tea corner and TOFU CAFE FUJINO, and a counter at JR Kyoto Isetan. A September 2026 guest returned for dinner after about 25 years.
chef_bio.philosophy: Only domestic soybeans, 100% (official site).

anecdotes.text: A July 2026 diner asked for a second helping of the warm oboro tofu.
An October 2026 visitor took a number 20 minutes before opening and still missed the window seats.

kyoto_kyoto_bistro_park_hyatt.gf_detail: Ask. Bistro menu with pasta, a katsu sandwich and cream puffs (2025–26 reviews); no gluten information. One July 2026 diner’s advance request to change sauces was not carried through, so confirm any request on the day.
kyoto_kyoto_bistro_park_hyatt.vegan_detail: Ask. Tabelog lists vegetarian options; no vegan information.
kyoto_kyoto_bistro_park_hyatt.hours_raw: Lunch 11:30–17:00, dinner 17:00–21:00 (last order 20:00), daily; breakfast 7:30–10:30 is for hotel guests only (Tabelog). kyoto_kyoto_bistro_park_hyatt.notes: [Hotel bistro and café · Ninenzaka, Park Hyatt Kyoto’s casual room] The Park Hyatt’s all-day bistro looking onto Ninenzaka, with kimono-clad strollers outside: cream puffs (¥770), a Daye-pork katsu sandwich, seafood linguine and bistro plates, with no service charge. Most guests are from overseas and many staff speak English. Seating is timed — 90 min at lunch. Reviewers find it casual for the hotel, with strong flavours. 11:30–21:00 daily.

chef_bio.background: Per Tabelog: Park Hyatt Kyoto’s bistro, café and bar, opened 30 October 2019, facing Ninenzaka. A February 2026 review describes a four-day collaboration dinner in January–February 2026 with the guest chef Stéphane Pantel, whose own restaurant had closed the previous summer.

anecdotes.text: A September 2025 visitor counted about 80% overseas guests and many staff fluent in English or several languages, though a soft-serve arrived melted after waiting by the kitchen.
A January 2026 visitor rated the katsu sandwich above Maisen’s and called the price unbelievable next to Tokyo.
A July 2026 group arranged sauce changes in advance for a guest who dislikes onions, and found the request was not carried through on the day.

kyoto_ueto.vegan_detail: Ask. Gin and tonics with sansho and herbs, natural wine and non-alcoholic cocktails; the snacks use egg (2023–26 reviews).

kyoto_ueto.notes: [Bar · Higashiyama Sanjo, sansho gin and tonics from 2 pm] A calm, tea-house-like bar a minute from Higashiyama Stn that opens in the afternoon (from 14:00). Gin and tonics with fresh sansho infused into the gin, flower-sansho and kinome, natural wines, a pudding and a sansho tartar egg dog. chef_bio.background: Per Tabelog: a bar, café and wine bar opened 8 April 2011. A February 2023 review calls it "Ueto salon & bar", with a tea-house-like interior and a woodworkers’ workshop space on the floor above.

anecdotes.text: A June 2026 visitor was shown the bottle of gin with fresh sansho steeping in it, giving the G&T its spicy kick.

kyoto_shokudo_days.notes: [Yoshoku · Shijo Kawaramachi, booked-out white omurice] A bright second-floor room just south of Shijo whose "white" omurice — pale eggs that run over demi-glace chicken rice, ¥1,760 — fills every lunch slot, so book (calls go through outside opening hours). roles: Owner-chef (unnamed), trained at top hotels in Kobe and Kyoto (October 2025 review)

kyoto_senbon_tamajuken.hours_raw: Mon, Tue, Thu–Sun 8:30–17:00; closed Wednesday (Tabelog). kyoto_senbon_tamajuken.notes: [Wagashi · Senbon Imadegawa, a Nishijin confectioner since 1938] A wagashi house on the weaving streets of Nishijin, founded in 1938 and now run by the third generation, making over a hundred seasonal namagashi a year with the sweetness turned down for today’s tastes. Take home Nishijin Fumi or the day’s namagashi, or sit at the tea room 茶寮SENTAMA next door for a fresh sweet with matcha (¥700). Closed Wednesday.

chef_bio.background: Per the official site: the 玉壽軒 name began in the late-Edo Kansei era with 井筒屋, a tapestry weaver just below the present site that sold penny sweets on the side; in the mid-Taisho era road widening moved the old shop to Imadegawa Omiya. The previous owner, who trained at 本家玉壽軒, set up independently in 1938 (昭和13年) on the original site as 千本玉壽軒; the third generation now runs it, keeping traditional methods and natural ingredients while lowering the sweetness. The tea room 茶寮SENTAMA opened next door in October 2020.
chef_bio.philosophy: Traditional methods with natural ingredients, adjusted to modern tastes (official site).

anecdotes.text: A July 2024 regular praised the summer sweets inspired by the halberd (hoko).
A September 2024 buyer found the Tsuki no Utage wasanbon so hard it would not break in half, and let it dissolve instead.
A March 2026 visitor at 茶寮SENTAMA watched the sweets being made at the counter and found the renovated room spotless.

kyoto_coffee_pocket.notes: [Kissa · Karasuma Oike, a postwar family coffee shop] A red-awninged Showa coffee shop by the Manga Museum, run by a kind couple: ¥400 coffee and mixed sandwiches on multigrain bread, a ¥850 morning set. The sign famously lacks its "T." Smoking is allowed at every seat, and it is cash only. Closed Sunday.

chef_bio.chef_name: Keizo (second-generation owner, per an October 2025 review)
roles: Run by a husband and wife (January 2025; October 2025; August 2026)
chef_bio.background: Per an October 2025 diner: founded in 1945 by Setsuko Taniguchi, who fled the air raids with her mother, moved from Kobe to Kyoto and opened the shop just after the war, first selling sweet red-bean soup made from black-market beans; she ran it for 58 years, and in 2011 her eldest son Keizo became the second-generation owner. The same diner relays the story that the wooden "Pocket" sign lacks its "T," to be added when the shop makes its mother proud. Reviewers in 2025–2026 describe a kind couple, red chairs and wooden tables, a television, and an elderly owner (June 2026).

anecdotes.text: "This charming, traditional coffee shop is run by a husband and wife team." — January 2025.
October 2025: the missing "T" in the wooden sign "symbolizes that when the café becomes a place that makes its mother proud, the 'T' will finally be added."
"The smell of tobacco hits my nostrils. Non-smokers might find it uncomfortable." — June 2024.

Courses about ¥10,000. Diners call it good value for the beef; one found portions small, the room cramped and the service unsmiling (April 2024). Open nightly until 23:30.

chef_bio.background: Opened 1 September 2020 (Tabelog). The shop’s Tabelog blurb calls it not a high-end place but a small one that never compromises on meat: A5 heifers fattened 38 to 50 months, from producers such as Okazaki Farm (pure Tajima-Omi beef) and Nishizawa (Kobe beef), grilled over binchotan in a quiet machiya. Reviewers note whole-cattle buying that brings rare cuts at fair prices, a Nishijin-woven exterior, and anniversary plates.
chef_bio.philosophy: Tabelog blurb: a small yakiniku that pursues the essence of long-term fattening.
chef_bio.specialty: Sea urchin and tongue yukhoe; Omi beef comparison platter.

anecdotes.text: April 2024: the meat was delicious but portions "might be a bit lacking," the room "quite cramped," and the female staff picked up plates "without a smile" — and the anniversary message was origami with marker pen.
An April 2025 diner compared Kobe, Omi and Matsusaka side by side: "The Matsusaka Beef was particularly delicious!"
